changes: Item 1, SPEC.md l.5042 (§17.1 O12 default cell, single-line row, pipes unchanged): 'keep x = 0 (i): <reasons>; the lead's recommendation for now, revisit if playtests or telemetry show players moving swords off the centre plane for a tier' -> 'keep x = 0 (i), as built and as the approved SPEC has it (Q3), applied until Louis decides: <same reasons>. The lead recommends (ii): one arrow-key press at the default Move step (0.05, §11.6, §12.9) plays the Starter Sword (F5) Hard on two steps while the forged item looks the same (§13.7), and (ii) moves no plausible design a tier; its price is that a hilt built off-centre makes a straight blade read lopsided (A27)'. Why it is true: (i) is what the code does, and Q3 puts symmetry on x = 0. §11.6 says arrow keys nudge by the Move step, and §12.9 sets snap.move's default step to 0.05. Measured on 4ab556c: F5 moved ±0.05 goes Hammering 0.1037 -> 0.2250 and Sharpening 0.0989 -> 0.3030, both Hard. §13.7: a forged item renders from its own bounds. (ii) on all 33,109 valid plausible designs: no tier changes. A27 goes 0.0989 Normal -> 0.2391 Hard. The recommendation follows the shift journal (17 Nov 23:15), PROGRESS.md and DECISIONS.md.

The default is (i), as built and as the SPEC you approved has it, and the game keeps it until you decide. One arrow-key press (0.05 stud at the editor's default step) changes the Starter Sword's tier while the forged sword looks the same, and (ii) changed no sample sword's tier; its price is that a hilt built off to one side makes a straight blade read lopsided (A27).' Item 2, SPEC.md l.935-936 (§4.3, refilled l.935-943, same line count): 'So no hidden part chooses who owns another hidden part's overlap (an exact copy aside, below), but it can change how that overlap is measured' -> 'So no hidden part moves another part's place in the order that decides who owns an overlap, but it can change how another hidden part's overlap is measured'. Why it is true: MassProps.ownership sorts by kept, then rankOf[slot], then Sampling.measureRanked. Each part's keys are its own, and a cleaned part is placed from the kept parts' centre, so a hidden part takes overlap only through its own place. Measured with order.luau: V1a and V1aNear put the copy above 18 and 17, and the other 14 parts keep their order and kept flags while own18 drops 0.01397844 -> 0.00162712. In a sweep of 2,242 added hidden parts, every other part's order is unchanged. The aside is dropped because an exact copy moves no other part's place either.

Item 2, SPEC.md l.1145-1146 (§4.4 cleaned-parts paragraph, refilled l.1145-1149, same line count): 'so not for which of two other cleaned parts owns their overlap (§4.3)' -> 'so not for another part's place in the order that decides who owns an overlap (§4.3)'. Same code reading and measurements as §4.3.

Item 2, SPEC.md l.5054 (§17.2 S2 hidden-parts row, in place, pipes unchanged): 'nor which of two hidden parts owns their overlap, and so the mass and balance shown' -> 'nor which of two other hidden parts comes first in the order that decides who owns their overlap, and so the mass and balance shown'. Same evidence. It also follows the row's own sentence, 'No hidden part moves another part's place in either rank'.

Item 2, README.md l.148 (Status paragraph, refilled l.148-166, same line count): 'chooses which of two hidden parts owns their overlap, and with it the mass and balance shown' -> 'chooses which of two other hidden parts comes first in the order that decides who owns their overlap, and with it the mass and balance shown'. Same evidence.

Item 3, SPEC.md l.998 (§4.4 Rank paragraph): 'a hair lower or a hair smaller, is cleaned' -> 'a hair lower or a hair smaller inside its original, is cleaned'. Measured with the round-9 checker's chk9 E1 on 4ab556c: Wedge copies cut by 1e-4 in every size (F3 p7, C08 p5 and p6, F4 p5, into the Grip, Guard or Pommel) poke out and are kept, in 12 cases. Smaller copies that lie inside their original are cleaned.

Item 3, SPEC.md l.1000-1001: 'in one whose name comes first it takes over' -> 'in one whose name comes first a copy of the same volume takes over'. Why it is true: Sampling.ranked compares volume before the slot's name. V2's classcheck8 A on 4ab556c: in a first-named slot, all 30 same-volume variants take over (copy kept, original cleaned, steps equal to the part relabelled in 30 of 30). None of the 10 hair-smaller copies takes over.

Item 3, SPEC.md l.1002-1007 (Rank paragraph refilled l.998-1031, 3 lines longer): 'so its label counts, exactly as relabelling the part it encloses would (F3's ...; §17.2).' -> 'so its label counts as relabelling the part it encloses would, with its own size measured: in every case tried the verdicts and tiers are the relabelled part's, the numbers not always (F3's ...; C15's guard crossbar with a copy 1e-12 larger in the Blade: Sharpening 0.4291 → 0.3404 Hard, where relabelling it gives 0.5329 Hard; §17.2).' Why it is true: the measure reads kept parts only, so it reads the encloser's own geometry. c15v.luau on 4ab556c: the copy is kept and part 3 hidden; Sharpening is 0.3404 at 1e-12, 1e-9 and 1e-6 (0.3403 at 1e-4) against 0.5329 relabelled, and every step's tier is the same. The round-9 checker found the same verdicts and tiers as relabelling in 2,380 of 2,380 cases.

Item 4, .build-notes/m3/M3-spec-changes.md l.687 (Round 7 item, refilled l.687-691, same line count): '...so a guard piece's copy relabelled grip takes the guard piece's place.' -> '..., takes the guard piece's place, and in one slot iron before steel.' (V2 r8 minor 6's words, appended to the sentence as V2 wrote them). Why it is true: for exact copies Sampling.ranked runs volume, slot name, place, sorted extents, then the material's name. V2's copyrule8 on all its builds on 4ab556c: for a kept original with a copy in the same slot in the other material, the copy whose material's name comes first stays visible in 113 of 113 cases (11 copies, 102 originals).

Item 5, .build-notes/m3/M3-spec-changes.md l.274-276 (refilled, same line count): 'enclosed parts, duplicates, dust' -> 'enclosed parts, plain duplicates (same slot and material), dust'. Why it is true: T-DIF-04's duplicates are Gen.withFiller's Duplicate, Gen.copyPart(host), which keeps the host's slot and material. A copy in an earlier-named slot takes over and can move D (§4.4).

Item 5, docs/spec/SPEC-evidence.md l.3946 (in place, 120 columns): '04 enclosed, duplicates and dust bit-identical' -> '04 enclosed, plain duplicates and dust bit-identical'. Same reason. The T-PHY 09 entry just above already reads 'copies of one slot and material'.

Item 6, src/shared/Physics/MassProps.luau l.386-387, comment only: '-- an exact copy of a part already above adds nothing to the union, so a Ctrl+D copy left in place / -- changes no part's count of higher parts, its overlap box or the cleaned parts' budget' -> '-- an exact copy of a part already in H adds nothing to their union, so it is not added again: of a / -- part and its copy left in place, the later in §4.3's priority adds nothing (owning 0, below)'. Why it is true: the loop skips q whenever Shapes.sameSolid(q, H[t]); sameSolid compares geometry only, so any slot or material counts. The earlier part of a pair is in the later one's H, so the copy check below gives the later one V_own 0, and the sort order is §4.3's priority. The old words were false when the copy comes first (V1a: the copy joins 18's higher parts). The 580 non-comment lines are byte-identical and the line count is unchanged; the new lines are 119 and 115 columns at tab 4.

summary:
All seven points are fixed in the working tree, and nothing is committed. Each changed sentence was checked against the code and against fresh measurements on 4ab556c, reusing the reviewers' scripts plus one new script of my own.

- **O12 (item 1):** the SPEC's default cell and the plain words now both say that (i) is the default (as built and as approved) until Louis decides, and that the lead recommends (ii). The reason given is that one arrow-key press moves the Starter Sword to Hard on two steps while the forged sword looks the same, and that (ii) changes no tier on any of the 33,109 valid sample swords. The price given is A27's off-centre hilt, which makes its straight blade read lopsided. No other statement of the lead's O12 recommendation exists in the texts.
- **Who owns an overlap (item 2):** §4.3, §4.4, §17.2's hidden-parts row and the README now all say it by the order: no hidden part moves another part's place in the order that decides who owns an overlap. The '(an exact copy aside, below)' aside is gone. On 2,242 added hidden parts, V1a and V1aNear included, no other part's place moved.
- **§4.4 (item 3):** 'a hair smaller' is now 'inside its original'. The take-over clause is limited to 'a copy of the same volume'. The encloser sentence drops 'exactly' and adds C15's 0.3404 against 0.5329.
- **Items 4 and 5:** the plain words add 'and in one slot iron before steel', and both T-DIF-04/05 summaries now say 'plain duplicates'.
- **Items 6 and 7:** the MassProps comment and the T-DIF-04 case name now say what the code and the case actually do. The code is unchanged outside the comment lines.

`--quick`: 865 pass, 0 fail, 30.67 s at a median 14.7 % load. `--filter "T-DIF-04"`: 16 pass, 13.07 s at a median 13.4 %. The layout checks pass.

One open point for you: SPEC §4.5 and the MassProps header comment still use the old ownership wording. They were outside the four places listed, so I left them.
